name: discord-social-mcp
description: Discord (social): me, publish_text, read_comments, reply_comment, delete, publish_image. Every tool

platform_mcp_discord_bot_token.title: PLATFORM_MCP_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN
platform_mcp_discord_bot_token.description: Bot token from the app's Bot page in the Developer Portal, pasted WITHOUT the 'Bot ' prefix: the runtime adds it and sends 'Authorization: Bot <token>' ('authentication is performed with the Authorization HTTP header in the format Authorization: TOKEN_TYPE TOKEN', https://docs.discord.com/developers/reference#authentication). Channel permissions needed: VIEW_CHANNEL + READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY (read_comments), SEND_MESSAGES (publish_text, reply_comment), MANAGE_MESSAGES to delete other users' messages; the MESSAGE_CONTENT privileged intent to read other users' message content. Same field as the messaging entry (env PLATFORM_MCP_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN).

platform_mcp_discord_channel_id.title: PLATFORM_MCP_DISCORD_CHANNEL_ID
platform_mcp_discord_channel_id.description: Snowflake id of the guild text / announcement channel (or forum-post thread) the bot publishes to (Discord client: User Settings > Advanced > Developer Mode, then right-click the channel > Copy Channel ID). The social vocabulary carries no channel argument, so publish_text, reply_comment and delete all address /channels/<channel_id>/messages; env PLATFORM_MCP_DISCORD_CHANNEL_ID.

tools.name: me
tools.description: GET /users/@me 'Returns the user object of the requester's account' - for a bot token the bot's own user (id, username, discriminator, global_name, bot: true).

tools.name: publish_text
tools.description: POST /channels/{channel.id}/messages ('Post a message to a guild text or DM channel') into the configured channel_id; `text` is `content` ('Message contents (up to 2000 characters)'). `reply_to` (a message id in the same channel) is sent as message_reference.message_id ('Replies are created by including a message_reference when sending a message. The referenced message must exist or the request will fail with HTTP error 400' - an upstream_error). Returns the message object: `id` is the message id, which identifies the post only together with the channel it lives in (delete uses the configured channel_id); `created_at` is the ISO-8601 `timestamp`; Discord messages carry no url. Needs SEND_MESSAGES (plus READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY for replies).

tools.name: read_comments
tools.description: `post_id` is a CHANNEL or THREAD id, not a message id: Discord has no per-message reply list, but a thread is addressed like a channel and a thread started from a message shares that message's id ('The id of the created thread will be the same as the id of the source message, and as such a message can only have a single thread created from it', https://docs.discord.com/developers/resources/channel#start-thread-from-message), so passing a forum post's id (or any thread id) lists the replies in that thread; passing a text channel id lists the channel. GET /channels/{channel.id}/messages: 'Retrieves the messages in a channel. Returns an array of message objects from newest to oldest on success.' `limit` is 'Max number of messages to return (1-100)', default 50; Discord pages by message id (before / after / around), so `page` is ignored and only the newest `limit` messages are returned. Needs VIEW_CHANNEL + READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY ('If the current user is missing the READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY permission in the channel, then no messages will be returned'), and other users' `content` is empty without the MESSAGE_CONTENT intent. `author` is author.username (id under raw.author.id).

tools.name: reply_comment
tools.description: A reply is a Create Message carrying message_reference.message_id = comment_id ('Replies are created by including a message_reference when sending a message'), posted into the configured channel_id - so the comment must live in that channel (message_reference.channel_id is not sent, and 'The referenced message must exist or the request will fail with HTTP error 400'). Needs SEND_MESSAGES + READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY.

tools.name: delete
tools.description: DELETE /channels/{channel.id}/messages/{message.id} deletes the message `post_id` in the configured channel_id: 'Delete a message. The current user must be the author of the message or, if the message was in a guild channel, have the MANAGE_MESSAGES permission. Returns a 204 No Content response on success.' The runtime answers {status: 'deleted'}; a message that is not in the configured channel is a 404 (invalid_input).

tools.name: publish_image
tools.description: Create Message with `embeds` ('Up to 10 rich embeds'; 'at least one of content, embeds, files, sticker_ids, poll, or components' is required) into the configured channel_id: each image URL becomes one embed whose `image.url` is 'source url of image (only supports http(s) and attachments)' (Embed Image Structure {url, proxy_url?, height?, width?}); `text` is the message `content`. Up to FOUR image_urls are sent (embeds 0-3; more are ignored) - Discord itself must be able to fetch the URLs. Same response mapping as publish_text (id, created_at = timestamp; no url).
